whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Slack Consultant exam for?

personas.label: Implementation Consultants
personas.description: You help companies set up Slack workspaces, channels, and workflows for their teams.

personas.label: Change Management Specialists
personas.description: You guide people as they move from email and older tools to Slack, and track whether the change is working.

personas.label: Salesforce Consultants
personas.description: You connect Slack with Sales Cloud and Service Cloud so teams can work with Salesforce records in Slack.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Slack Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam covers how a consultant delivers Slack for a client: discovery, Enterprise Grid design, migration, policies and settings, channel strategy, governance, and helping people learn it.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
60 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
Seven sections. Policies and Settings (22%), Learning and Enablement (18%), and Delivery and Migration (17%) carry the most weight.
No prerequisite. Salesforce lists none for this exam.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Hands-on experience with a Slack rollout, including training and adoption, can help. Aim for at least 80% on practice tests before booking.

examFormat.heading: Slack Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Many questions describe a company situation and ask what a consultant should recommend.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions may cover a merger, a security requirement, or low adoption. Look for the company’s goal and constraints before choosing a recommendation.
bestWayToPass: Learn Slack structure: Review workspaces, Enterprise Grid, channels, and Slack Connect for work with outside organizations.
Compare automation tools: Learn Workflow Builder triggers and steps, and when Salesforce Flow is a better fit.
Study Salesforce integration: Know how the Salesforce apps for Slack show records and send alerts into channels.
Plan for adoption: Review champions, training, clear channel rules, and ways to measure success.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers planning and running a Slack rollout: workspace and channel design, workflows, Salesforce integration, security, governance, and user adoption. The exam is 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 67% pass mark, weighted towards Policies and Settings (22%) and Learning and Enablement (18%).

keyConcepts.h2: Slack Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Salesforce and Slack Integration
blocks.body: The **Salesforce apps for Slack** let people search, view, and update records and receive alerts without leaving Slack. **Salesforce Flow** can post to a channel or create a channel after an event, such as a large deal closing. Teams can use a channel for an account or major case so everyone can coordinate in one place. **Agentforce** and other AI features can also work in Slack. Use the simplest option that meets the need, and keep Salesforce as the system of record.

blocks.heading: Slack for Customer Service
blocks.body: Support teams can use **swarming** when a case is difficult: an agent brings experts into a Slack channel linked to the case so they can work on it together. Teams can send alerts about urgent cases or missed service targets to the right channel. Useful answers from these discussions may later become Knowledge articles. The goal is to help customers faster and reduce email follow-ups between agents.

blocks.heading: Workflow Builder and Salesforce Flow
blocks.body: **Workflow Builder** lets people create simple no-code workflows in Slack, such as a request form that posts to a channel for approval. A workflow starts with a **trigger**, such as a shortcut, a new channel member, or a schedule, then runs **steps**, which may connect to other apps. Use **Salesforce Flow** when a process changes Salesforce data or needs complex rules. It can send results to Slack. Assign owners to workflows and review them so unused workflows do not build up.

blocks.heading: Data Governance and Compliance
blocks.body: Admins use **retention policies** to set how long messages and files are kept. **Legal holds** and **eDiscovery** support legal requests. **Data loss prevention** can detect sensitive information, such as payment card numbers, in messages. **Enterprise Key Management** lets a company manage its encryption keys, and **data residency** keeps data in a selected region. Use **SSO** for sign-in and **SCIM** to create or remove user accounts from the company identity system. Set clear rules for channel creation and invitations to outside users.

blocks.heading: Adoption and Change Management
blocks.body: A Slack rollout works only when people use it. Start with clear goals and a few useful cases, such as moving project discussions out of email. Recruit **champions** in each team to help coworkers. Set **channel naming rules** and explain when to use channels or direct messages. Offer short training that relates to people’s work. Track active users, channel messages compared with DMs, and changes in internal email use. Adjust the plan based on what you learn.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Slack Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Questions describe a company’s goals or limits. Identify the real problem first; the best answer may be a change to people or processes, not a new feature.

blocks.heading: Choose Useful First Use Cases
blocks.body: Start with a few important use cases that support business goals. Expand after teams have learned what works.

blocks.heading: Choose the Right Workflow Tool
blocks.body: Use Workflow Builder for simple Slack processes. Use Salesforce Flow when the process changes Salesforce data or needs complex logic.

blocks.heading: Connect Slack with Salesforce
blocks.body: Bring relevant records and alerts into channels where teams work, and keep Salesforce as the source of truth.

blocks.heading: Support Adoption
blocks.body: Use champions, training, clear channel rules, and goals you can measure. Adding features alone rarely solves low adoption.

blocks.heading: Set Governance Rules
blocks.body: Review retention, legal holds, data loss prevention, SSO, SCIM, channel creation, and external sharing.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Consultant Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Slack Consultant:

sampleQuestions.question: An agency needs to work with a company in shared Slack channels. It does not want the company’s users added to its own workspace. What should it use?
options: Create a separate Slack workspace for the outside agency.
Give each agency worker a guest account in the company workspace.
Use Slack Connect to share channels between workspaces.
Set up one shared email inbox for both organizations.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack Connect lets organizations share channels while each keeps its own workspace and admin controls.
whyWrong: A separate workspace would split the conversation and add setup work.
Guest accounts place outside users in the company workspace and require extra administration.
This is the feature for shared channels across separate organizations.

sampleQuestions.question: Sales reps want a Slack alert when a Salesforce Opportunity over $1 million closes. What should the team set up?
options: Use Salesforce Flow to post the alert to the team channel.
Ask each rep to post a message manually after a deal closes.
Send a report by email at the end of each day.
Build a Workflow Builder form for reps to submit the closed deal.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce Flow can respond to the Opportunity update and post a message to the Slack channel.
whyWrong: Manual posts may be forgotten and do not automate the alert.
A daily email arrives later and is not a channel alert.
A form needs someone to submit it; it does not react to the record change.

sampleQuestions.question: Employees send IT requests by direct message, so requests are hard to track. What no-code solution could a consultant recommend?
options: Ban direct messages without providing another way to request help.
Have developers build a custom Slack app for the request process.
Hold a weekly meeting to collect requests from employees.
Use a Workflow Builder form in the IT channel.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workflow Builder can collect requests in a form and post them to an IT channel for the team to track.
whyWrong: Banning DMs does not create a replacement request process.
A custom app is more work than needed for a simple no-code process.
A weekly meeting delays requests and makes tracking difficult.

sampleQuestions.question: Legal requires messages in selected channels to be kept for seven years. What should the consultant configure?
options: A naming rule to mark channels with legal messages.
Slack Connect settings for those channels.
Retention policies for the selected channels.
A Workflow Builder step that reminds people to save messages.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retention policies control how long messages and files are kept.
whyWrong: A naming rule does not affect how long Slack keeps messages.
Slack Connect supports external collaboration, not message retention.
A reminder does not set or enforce a retention period.

sampleQuestions.question: When employees leave, their Slack accounts should be removed automatically. What should the company set up?
options: A retention policy for each departing user.
SCIM provisioning connected to the identity provider.
A monthly manual review to remove former employees.
A naming rule for accounts that should be disabled.
sampleQuestions.explanation: SCIM can automatically create and remove Slack accounts through the company’s identity system.
whyWrong: Retention policies govern data, not user account access.
A monthly manual check may leave former users active in the meantime.
Naming rules do not deactivate user accounts.

sampleQuestions.question: Six months after a Slack rollout, many teams still use email for projects. What should the consultant focus on first?
options: Turn off company email so teams have to use Slack.
Install more apps to encourage teams to change tools.
Buy more Slack licenses for every employee.
Improve adoption with champions, guidance, and training.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Low use is often an adoption issue. Champions and clear guidance can help people change how they work.
whyWrong: Turning off email can disrupt work without teaching teams how to use Slack.
More apps do not necessarily help people change their habits.
More licenses do not ensure that people will use Slack.

sampleQuestions.question: Which measure best shows that teams are sharing work openly in Slack?
options: How many emoji reactions people use.
How many workspaces the company has.
The share of messages posted in channels rather than DMs.
How many apps have been installed in the workspace.
sampleQuestions.explanation: A higher share of channel messages shows that more work is visible to the team instead of staying in private messages.
whyWrong: Emoji use does not show whether work is shared openly.
The number of workspaces does not measure how teams communicate.
Installed apps do not show whether teams work in channels or DMs.

sampleQuestions.question: A support agent needs help from engineering with a complex case. What Slack approach fits?
options: Start a case channel and bring the needed experts together to swarm.
Email the entire engineering team and wait for responses.
Close the case and create a new one for engineering.
Wait until the next team meeting to raise the case.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Swarming brings the right people together in a channel linked to the case so they can resolve it faster.
whyWrong: Email is harder to follow and may delay the response.
Closing the case loses continuity and does not bring experts together.
Waiting for a meeting delays help for the customer.

sampleQuestions.question: Employees struggle to find channels because teams use different naming styles. What should the consultant recommend?
options: Set a clear channel naming convention with useful prefixes.
Create a separate workspace for every team.
Delete most channels without reviewing their use.
Move work conversations into direct messages.
sampleQuestions.explanation: A naming convention with prefixes, such as proj- or team-, helps people find channels.
whyWrong: A naming convention solves the discovery problem without splitting the workspace.
More workspaces do not fix unclear channel names.
Deleting channels can remove useful history and does not set a naming standard.

sampleQuestions.question: The company needs to detect credit card numbers posted in Slack messages. What should it use?
options: Data loss prevention rules that scan message content.
A naming convention for channels that discuss payments.
Huddles so payment details are discussed by voice.
A Workflow Builder form for IT requests.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data loss prevention can detect sensitive information, such as payment card numbers, in messages.
whyWrong: Channel names do not scan messages.
Huddles are for live audio or video conversations.
A request form does not scan workspace messages.

sampleQuestions.question: A company needs separate workspaces for business units and shared company-wide channels. What setup fits?
options: Use one channel for all employees in a single workspace.
Use Enterprise Grid to connect workspaces with central administration.
Use Slack Connect to link the company’s own business units.
Create workspaces that are not connected to each other.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enterprise Grid connects multiple company workspaces and supports central administration and shared channels.
whyWrong: One channel for everyone may not fit different business needs and does not provide separate workspaces.
Slack Connect is for collaboration between different organizations.
Unconnected workspaces cannot easily share company-wide channels.

sampleQuestions.question: A Slack approval must update several Salesforce records using complex rules. Which tool should handle the record logic?
options: Pin a message with the approval instructions.
Use Workflow Builder alone to update all Salesforce records.
Set a Slack reminder for the person who approves.
Use Salesforce Flow for the record logic.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce Flow can handle complex Salesforce record logic while Slack supports the approval interaction.
whyWrong: A pinned message stores information but does not automate record updates.
Workflow Builder is suited to simpler Slack-side processes, not complex Salesforce logic.
A reminder does not update Salesforce records.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to manage its own encryption keys for Slack data. Which feature should it use?
options: Slack Connect for shared-channel access.
Enterprise Key Management for encryption keys.
Retention policies for message storage periods.
SCIM provisioning for user accounts.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enterprise Key Management lets a company control the encryption keys used for its Slack data.
whyWrong: Slack Connect supports collaboration with external organizations.
Retention policies set how long data is kept.
SCIM manages user account provisioning.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a good first step when planning a Slack rollout?
options: Turn off email before teams start using Slack.
Install as many apps as possible before setting goals.
Set clear goals and choose a few valuable use cases.
Move every company tool into Slack on the first day.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Starting with clear goals and a few use cases creates quick wins and ways to measure progress.
whyWrong: Turning off email is disruptive and not required to start a rollout.
Installing many apps can add noise before teams know what they need.
Moving every tool at once can overwhelm employees.

sampleQuestions.question: Sales reps want to find and update Salesforce Opportunities without leaving Slack. What should the company set up?
options: Create a separate Workflow Builder form for every Opportunity.
Install and configure the Salesforce app for Slack.
Use a Slack reminder to link to the Salesforce records.
Post a daily export of Opportunities to a channel.
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Salesforce app for Slack lets users find, view, and update records from Slack.
whyWrong: A separate form for each Opportunity would be hard to maintain.
A reminder does not provide a way to work with the record.
This app supports Salesforce record work inside Slack.

sampleQuestions.question: A client is merging three standalone workspaces into Enterprise Grid. What should happen before the migration is scheduled?
options: Delete all channels with fewer than ten members in each workspace
Ask every user to export their own direct message history first
Turn off single sign-on until all workspaces have been moved over
Clean up user accounts and send a communication plan to users
sampleQuestions.explanation: Pre-migration work includes scheduling, cleaning up user accounts, and telling users what will change and when.
whyWrong: Channel size is not a reason to delete content before a migration.
Users do not need to export their own messages for a workspace migration.
Disabling sign-in controls weakens security and is not a pre-migration step.

sampleQuestions.question: What should a consultant have agreed with the client by the end of discovery?
options: A final list of every channel the company will ever need
A completed migration of the client's largest workspace
A recorded training course for all future employees
A vision statement and measurable success metrics
sampleQuestions.explanation: Discovery ends with a shared vision for Slack and success metrics, which guide the design and show later whether the rollout worked.
whyWrong: Channel needs change over time; discovery does not fix a permanent list.
Migration happens later, after design and planning.
Learning materials are built later, in the enablement phase.

sampleQuestions.question: A company on Enterprise Grid wants an announcements channel that every employee in every workspace can see. What should the consultant recommend?
options: An org-wide channel shared across all workspaces
A Slack Connect channel shared with each workspace
A private channel recreated in every single workspace
A separate workspace that holds only announcements
sampleQuestions.explanation: On Enterprise Grid, a channel can be shared across some or all workspaces, so one org-wide channel reaches every employee.
whyWrong: Slack Connect is for working with outside organizations, not for a company's own workspaces.
Separate copies would split the announcements and have to be kept in step by hand.
An extra workspace adds overhead when one org-wide channel does the job.

sampleQuestions.question: Which role has the highest level of control over an Enterprise Grid organization?
options: Workspace Admin
Org Primary Owner
Channel Manager
Multi-Channel Guest
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Org Primary Owner sits at the top of the Enterprise Grid role hierarchy, above Org Owners, Org Admins, and the workspace-level roles.
whyWrong: A Workspace Admin manages one workspace, not the whole organization.
A Channel Manager manages settings for individual channels.
A guest has limited access to selected channels only.

sampleQuestions.question: Slack's experiential learning approach asks users to learn mainly by doing what?
options: Reading a policy document before getting access
Watching a long recorded lecture on their own
Practising real tasks in Slack during the session
Passing a written test on Slack terminology
sampleQuestions.explanation: Experiential learning has people use Slack while they learn, so they practise the habits they will need in daily work.
whyWrong: Reading alone is not hands-on practice.
A lecture is passive; experiential learning is active.
A terminology test checks recall, not the ability to work in Slack.
